top.title: Antonian volleyball aims to defend TAPPS Class 6A state championship
top.description: Antonian's Abby Ibarra (17) is embraced by teammates after scoring a point against the Incarnate Word Shamrocks during the second set Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026, at Antonian High School Gym in San Antonio. The Apaches swept the Shamrocks 25-11, 25-17, 25-13. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) One year after ending a championship dry spell, Antonian returns to the TAPPS state volleyball tournament eager for a chance to notch back-to-back titles. The Apaches (45-4) play Tomball Concordia Lutheran (13-19-1) in a Class 6A semifinal at 7 p.m. Friday at Robinson High School. The winner plays the victor of the Fort Worth Nolan and Plano Prestonwood match that precedes it. The title game is set for 4 p.m. Saturday at Robinson. Antonian is one of two local teams at the TAPPS state tournament. Boerne Geneva plays Bryan Brazos Christian in a 4A semifinal on Friday at Waco's McClennan Community College. Antonian returns an experienced team, including five starters from the squad that defeated Dallas Bishop Lynch in four sets in 2025 to win its first TAPPS state championship in eight years and its sixth overall. "From last season to now, we've definitely grown as a team, especially with all the new people that we have," senior middle blocker Maci Cantu said. "Honestly, I feel our chemistry is better than ever and I'm really confident going to state right now." Cantu, senior right side hitter Lucy Rote and sophomore outside hitter Jordyn Daniels return after earning all-tournament honors at state last season. Senior setter Camila Serna and junior outside hitter Abby Ibarra are also back. "State is the end goal and the end result," Serna said. "This team does a lot of hard work and a lot of work behind the scenes that works really well for us." Rote, a fourth-year starter, is especially grateful to be back. She spent most of the latter half of the season nursing a high ankle sprain after rolling it during practice in mid-September. She missed a month as a result. She returned Oct. 15 and has played eight sets in four matches. Because high ankle sprains are notoriously slow to heal, Rote was initially concerned about not being healthy enough to return before season's end. "There was always a little doubt that there was going to be a chance that I wasn't going to be able to come back," Rote said. "That upset me, but doing my rehab and doing my physical therapy was what made me come back so quick. And I came back at a good time. I've been able to practice a little bit and have some games before the state tournament." top.title: Here's where Golden State Valkyries players will play basketball this offseason
top.description: The Valkyries' Gabby Williams drinks champagne at the parade in San Francisco, Nov. 4, 2026. (Douglas Zimmerman/SFGATE) While it's officially the offseason for the Golden State Valkyries , most of the team is doing anything but taking time off from basketball. Top WNBA players often compete year-round, traveling across the world at times to play for teams that can sometimes pay them a higher salary than they make in the league. While there have been domestic ventures aiming to keep players in the United States during the offseason, the fact remains that the grind as a professional women's basketball player hardly stops. But that's good news for the fans who are undoubtedly itching to see their favorite players, and newly minted champions, take the floor again as soon as possible. There are five Valkyries players who plan to remain stateside for Unrivaled , a three-on-three women's basketball league founded by WNBA stars Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier, who is rumored to be a free agent target for Golden State . The league plays its regular season on a touring-style schedule throughout different arenas across the country, and two games are even scheduled to take place on Jan. 11 at Chase Center. Gabby Williams is scheduled to play for the Laces (and be joined by her partner, Marine Johannes), Kaitlyn Chen for the Breeze (alongside her former UConn teammate Paige Bueckers), Veronica Burton for the Mist, Tiffany Hayes for the Phantom and Kayla Thornton for the Rose. Kaila Charles is also slated to to play in Unrivaled, though she's one of six in the "player pool" that will be used to help fill in for injuries on other rosters. Then there's the overseas contingency. Rookie Juste Jocyte is signed to compete in the international basketball league startup Project B . The women's league, which has attracted a fair amount of WNBA talent , is scheduled to begin in China in January and to play their games in cities around the world like Tokyo and Valencia, Spain. Cecilia Zandalasini plans to head back home to compete for Italian team Schio . Janelle Salaun, the reigning Sixth Player of the Year and most prominent player to miss the San Francisco parade , is signed up to play for Galatasaray in Turkey. Aminata Gueye signed a deal in June to play for Czech team ZVVZ USK Praha . Development players Ashten Prechtel and Miela Sowah are also both playing internationally. Prechtel is currently competing in Japan for Eneos Sunflowers, which caused her to also miss Wednesday's parade, and Sowah is scheduled to compete in Australia for the Townsville Fire. The three unknowns as of Thursday afternoon are Laeticia Amihere, Kiah Stokes and Iliana Rupert, although Rupert missed this past season because of her pregnancy. top.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $76,000 as Nasdaq Tumbles into Correction
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $76,000 as Nasdaq Tumbles into Correction Bitcoin price traded near $76,000 on Thursday afternoon, down more than 5% on the day after sliding through the mid-$75,000s as a Nasdaq-led selloff in chip and AI stocks deepened into a formal correction and forced out more than $1 billion in leveraged bets, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The afternoon session extended the morning crash that had already erased overnight gains above $80,000. Bitcoin briefly tested support near $75,400 before stabilizing just under $76,000 into the final hour of U.S. cash trading. Bitcoin near $75,900 in afternoon trade, on track for its biggest single-day slide since June. The move undid Wednesday’s short-squeeze bounce in a single session. Traders who bought the midterm rebound with borrowed money were the first forced out when stocks cracked at the open, and the bitcoin price never regained the $77,000 area that held as morning support. Nasdaq’s correction pulls crypto lower Wall Street set the tone. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% on Thursday and dropped into correction territory, more than 10% below the record close it set last month, CNBC reported. The S&P 500 lost roughly 4%, and the Dow shed more than 1,600 points. Semiconductors led the rout. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index sank about 11%, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF posted its biggest one-day drop since March 2020. Nvidia and Broadcom each fell around 9%, Qualcomm lost about 9% and Tesla dropped about 11%. Investors are pricing in a slower AI data-center buildout under a Democratic Congress. Traders fear construction pauses and tighter financing for neoclouds, a risk that has weighed on chip and infrastructure names since the midterm results. Analysts told CNBC that the $1.2 trillion of AI capital spending forecast for next year is now being reworked. Bitcoin has moved with that AI-heavy complex for most of the year. Miners that sold bitcoin to fund data centers are now caught in both trades, so political risk on power and construction hits the same names that used to trade mainly on the bitcoin price. Leverage flush grows past $1 billion Forced selling kept the bitcoin price under pressure into the afternoon. Roughly $1.08 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including about $954 million in long bets, as futures markets unwound positions built during Wednesday’s short squeeze. Nearly $900 million of that wipeout came in a roughly four-hour stretch after the U.S. open, turning a stock-led break into a cascade of margin calls. Ether fell below $2,300 as the same leverage flushed out. Crypto equities followed. Strategy (MSTR), Coinbase (COIN) and Circle (CRCL) each fell more than 10%, and bitcoin miners dropped as much as 20%. top.title: Tottenham chief reveals ultimate aim to win the Premier League as he insists club is on 'right track'
top.description: Tottenham chief executive Vinai Venkatesham believes the club is heading in the right direction again and has outlined an ultimate objective of winning the Premier League . Spurs narrowly avoided a disastrous drop to the Championship during a tumultuous 2025-26 campaign that saw long-standing chairman Daniel Levy leave, while Thomas Frank and Igor Tudor were both sacked before Roberto De Zerbi secured survival on the final day. A summer of heavy spending followed, bringing 10 new signings and several high-profile departures. After a sluggish opening to the campaign, Tottenham travel to Leeds on Saturday on the back of three straight victories. Speaking on The Sports Agents Podcast, Venkatesham said: "We’ve had three better results in a row, but there is nothing here where we think, ‘oh we’ve cracked it’ and we’re right at the start of this journey of where we are going to. Roberto De Zerbi's side have won three games in a row (PA) "There will be good moments this season and bad moments this season, but I firmly believe we’re on the right track to where we want to get to. "Ultimately, I guess the best way to answer your question (about targets) is what are we here for? We’re here to win, right? The people that we’ve attracted to the football club, the long list of people, everyone is here to win. "If you work for Tottenham, when we talk about being here to win, that means we’re here to win the Premier League. That’s what this football club wants to do. It wants to win the Premier League and it wants to be consistent in the Champions League and ultimately win the Champions League. "Can I tell you what year that’s going to happen in? Obviously I can’t but that’s what we’re aiming for and that’s what I want every single person that works for this club to think about every single day." Venkatesham also disclosed that preparing for relegation last season was necessary, stating: "To not make that plan would have been irresponsible." Xavi Simons is set to return to training later this month (Getty) Meanwhile, playmaker Xavi Simons is progressing in his recovery from a severe knee injury and should return to training in late November. The Netherlands international suffered anterior cruciate ligament damage during April's 1-0 victory at Wolves, missing the conclusion of Tottenham's survival battle. ACL injuries typically require a nine-month recovery period, but Simons remains ahead of schedule and is set for first-team contact training later this month after the international break. This opens up the possibility of a match return weeks before the end of the year, delivering a timely boost to De Zerbi.

top.title: Kimi Antonelli opens up on "very emotional" visit to Ayrton Senna's family estate
top.description: Motorsport photo 2026 Formula 1 champion Kimi Antonelli has opened up about his recent visit to Ayrton Senna's family home ahead of this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix. The Mercedes driver went to Fazenda Dois Lagos, the Senna family estate, on Tuesday, two days after clinching the F1 title in Mexico. He shared a photo of himself sitting in the Lotus 98T that Senna raced in 1986 and thanked the family for an "unforgettable day". Speaking to the media at Interlagos, Antonelli said the experience had been even more emotional than he expected it to be. "I was truly emotional," the Italian said. "A very, very special day, a day that I will remember forever. That's why I will always be thankful and grateful towards the Senna family for allowing me to see that, and to even sit in the car, which was very special. "It was an amazing day. I actually didn't want to leave. I tried to stay as long as I could there, because it was such a nice experience. The Senna family was very open about showing places where Ayrton used to spend most of his time. It was crazy to think. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes "When I was there, I was like, 'Wow, Ayrton was actually here. He was spending time in his room.' It was very emotional and a very, very special day." Antonelli was joined for the visit by his father, Marco, as well as Senna's nephew Bruno and nieces Bianca and Lalalli. Bruno later thanked the 20-year-old on Instagram for "the karting lesson", with the estate having its own kart track. He will also race this weekend with a special tribute helmet to Senna, 35 years since the Brazilian's first home win at Interlagos in 1991. "This one means a lot to me," Antonelli posted on social media alongside the special helmet design. "My special helmet for the weekend! A tribute to my idol and Brazil. I hope you guys like it as much as I do." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

The first College Football Playoff rankings created a debate Alabama cannot avoid: How much should one head-to-head result matter when the committee weighs a team’s full season? Alabama opened at No. 5 with a 6-2 record. Tennessee, also 6-2, landed at No. 13 after beating the Crimson Tide by 16 points. LSU is No. 14, also at 6-2, and Alabama visits the Tigers Saturday in a game that could quickly change the playoff conversation. The rankings are not final, and there are several weeks left for teams to improve their résumés. Still, the first reveal puts Alabama in an unusually visible position: a two-loss team ranked in the top five, with a recent head-to-head defeat to another two-loss team ranked eight places lower. The committee says it weighs the whole resume The selection committee says it evaluates a team’s full profile, including schedule strength, head-to-head results, results against common opponents and other relevant factors. Alabama’s ranking suggests the committee valued its broader résumé more highly than Tennessee’s victory in their meeting. But the gap is large enough to invite scrutiny, especially with both teams holding identical records. The committee will release another set of rankings next week. Alabama has time to improve its position, but the No. 5 placement has already raised the stakes for every remaining game. For LSU, the stakes are just as clear. The Tigers can beat a team the committee currently sees as a playoff contender and strengthen their own position at the same time. The first rankings are a snapshot, not a verdict. But the Alabama-Tennessee gap has made the committee’s criteria part of the story, and Saturday’s game gives both teams a chance to add evidence. top.title: A.J. Brown knee injury ‘raises some concerns’ about Patriots future
top.description: The New England Patriots trading first- and fourth-round draft picks to the Philadelphia Eagles for wide receiver A.J. Brown was a gamble. On the one hand, he was a proven No. 1 wide receiver capable of adding a new level of playmaking ability to what was one of the best offenses in football in 2025. On the other hand, he was heading into his age-29 season off of his least productive season in four years. Eight weeks into the season, the gamble has not paid off. Brown has appeared in just three games so far, catching nine passes for 101 yards. A bigger concern than his output, however, is his injury situation. Not only did he spend four games on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain, he also is currently dealing with a knee injury that has forced him to miss four straight practices and last Sunday’s win in Miami. While that knee injury has not prompted another move to IR, Brown’s short-term availability has been impacted. And beyond that, there are questions about his long-term outlook as well as addressed by ESPN’s Adam Schefter on Thursday morning. “Let’s go back to the offseason, when Philadelphia was shopping A.J. Brown and they were talking to teams,” Schefter said. “One of the reasons that I believe there wasn’t more interest was there were some teams that had some questions about his knee. In fact, when they were advanced discussions for a trade with the Los Angeles Rams that was at one point close to being completed … I think the Rams had some concerns about his knee. The concerns that other teams have had have now manifested themselves in New England this season. “It flared up. … The knee held him out last week, and the knee is threatening to hold him out this week. It’s a knee that I think raises some concerns as to how long he’s going to keep playing here in New England, and producing at a high level.” More Here: pic.twitter.com/qJbKrjlrr4 — Carlos A. Lopez (@LosTalksPats) November 5, 2026 Worries about Brown’s knee are nothing new. Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf himself spoke about them earlier this year. “It’s a factor, but we examined him,” Wolf said back in June. “He’s got a knee that has some wear and tear that we were aware of. Our training staff and medical staff signed off on it.” Regardless of his current availability issues, the Patriots moving on from Brown in the near future is not expected. His contract structure alone would likely prevent such a move from happening: if released next offseason, for example, New England would take on a dead cap charge of almost $26 million. For the time being, though, Brown remains with the Patriots and part of their 53-man roster. How quickly he can return to the field will be seen, though; one line of thinking is that he might be kept out through the team’s trip to Germany next week and into the Week 11 bye to get fully ready for the stretch run. Whether he will be, only time will tell.

top.description: Army heads into the 2026-27 men's basketball season a bit older, more experienced and with more focus, says third-year head coach Kevin Kuwik. "I think as you get older, you give yourself the best chance,'' he said. The Black Knights opened Monday with a respectable showing in an 84-50 loss at No. 2 Duke, and Army made its home debut against NCAA Div. III Mount Saint Mary from Newburgh on Thursday night, the first of 15 home games at West Point's Christl Arena. "I'm excited to take this journey and see what we can do,'' Kuwik said. Army is coming off an 11-21 season (in February losing eight of its final nine. "We hit the wall,'' Kuwik said) and 5-13 mark in the Patriot League, so it's no wonder the league's coaches picked Army for 10th place in the preseason poll. The Black Knights return 11 players and introduce five freshmen to the lineup. With so many veterans available for a change, the team spent time training and playing in Puerto Rico over the summer, providing valuable practice time and developing. "I think it was awesome,'' Kuwik said of the experience. "We're definitely ahead of the game a far as having that live experience for those 11 returnees.'' Kuwik believes his team can play offense with good pace and share the ball well and the hope is the team will defend better this season - the Black Knights primarily play man-to-man in the halfcourt. "I think that's probably the most important thing,'' he said. Last season, Army gave up 77 points a game (scoring 72) and allowed foes to shoot 47 percent from the field, slightly up from a season earlier. Senior captains Ryan Curry and Tate Laczkowski will start at point and center, respectively. Kevin McCarthy and Jason Holloway return to starting roles on the wings. Junior Jaden Ellis allows the team to go small while sophomore Dylan Benner makes them bigger. "Ryan has a ton of experience and played in some big moments and made some big shots,'' Kuwik said. Curry, a third-team Patriot all-star, led the team with 13 points a game and 76 3-pointers. "He's poised to have a great year, both on the ball and off the ball.'' The 6-foot-7 Benner has good handling skills for a big man and his ability to step out can stretch a defense. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the 4-4 Las Vegas Raiders head towards the NFL trade deadline, they could be looking to be both buyers and sellers. Adding long-term help while parting with rentals would make plenty of sense for this Raiders team. What could the Raiders look to add? With Fernando Mendoza already on the roster, and Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer locking down the tight end position, adding someone at wide receiver would make plenty of sense. That's why ESPN's Seth Walder believes the Raiders should target Jacksonville Jaguars first-round WR Brian Thomas Jr., who the Jaguars have seemingly "given up on" this season. Raiders linked to trade for Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr. "Who should they target? Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr.," Walder writes. "... The Jaguars have pretty much given up on Thomas, but he would become the clear No. 1 option in Las Vegas..." Thomas has not been a productive player during the 2026 season for the Jaguars. So far, Thomas has just 10 receptions for 117 yards and two touchdowns through Week 8. Jacksonville hasn't been using him all that much, especially with Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington, and Brenton Strange involved in the passing offense. Josh Cameron has even been utilized in this passing offense more than Thomas. Adding Thomas, who's seemingly become someone the Jaguars have given up on, would make a ton of sense for the Raiders. nigeria.description: By Ozioruva Aliu – BENIN CITY Member of the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee led by its chairman, Osaro Culture Iyamu were, on Thursday, attacked by some beverage sellers while trying to enforce ban on sales of fake, adulterated and unauthorised drinks along Mission Road in Benin City, the state capital. nigeria.title: Nigeria must deploy tollgates, technology to improve highway security – Musa
nigeria.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd), has advocated restoring tollgates on major highways and deploying modern technology to enhance highway security and help identify and track criminals. Musa noted that tollgates could play a valuable security role, especially with modern technology that can identify and track vehicles without requiring drivers to stop for manual payments. The minister made the remarks at the Abuja roundtable, “Promise to Proof: The Renewed Hope Conversation,” organised by the APC Progressive Strategy Roundtable. It was convened by the Executive Chairman/CEO of PICNG and EVs, Ismaeel Ahmed. Responding to concerns about highway security and a suggestion that motorists could contribute through security levies at tollgates, Musa described the reintroduction of tollgates as a good idea, noting that Nigeria might have made a mistake by dismantling them. He explained that modern tolling systems in other countries use technology to identify vehicles through their registration numbers, with payments processed electronically, adding that such systems could also assist security agencies in identifying and tracking vehicles. The minister also called for the strengthening of Nigeria’s identification system through the use of personal identification numbers, facial recognition and fingerprints to improve security monitoring. He said technology would make it easier for security agencies to establish people’s identities and track criminal activities. On the broader security situation, Musa said the Federal Government was recording progress in tackling terrorism, banditry and kidnapping through increased defence investment, improved intelligence gathering, joint military operations and stronger cooperation among security agencies. He disclosed that the Federal Government allocated ₦5.4 trillion to defence in the 2026 budget and was recruiting an additional 12,000 military personnel to strengthen manpower and security coverage. According to him, the government was also investing in modern weapons, surveillance systems and operational platforms to improve intelligence gathering, mobility, firepower and rapid response capabilities. He further disclosed that Nigerian security forces killed more than 300 terrorists and bandits, including over 10 commanders, in operations conducted in the week preceding his presentation. The minister identified porous borders as a major challenge, noting that Nigeria shares extensive borders with neighbouring countries, particularly Niger Republic, through which criminal groups and illicit arms can move. He said the government was strengthening border security and expanding bilateral, regional and international defence cooperation through intelligence sharing, specialised training and technological support. nigeria.title: Italian chef sacked for refusing to put pineapple on pizza, says it insulted his culture
nigeria.description: An Italian chef in Australia has lost an unfair dismissal claim after being sacked for, among other workplace issues, refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, describing the topping as an insult to his culture. Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane in May, following a meeting with management over several complaints about his conduct. One of the issues raised was his refusal to prepare ham and pineapple pizzas for guests attending an event at the restaurant. According to a ruling by Australia’s Fair Work Commission, Tamburella argued that instructions from management “need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture”. The commission noted that the chef’s objection to the fruit was because “he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture”. It also found that this was not the first time he had refused to use pineapple on pizzas, recording three such instances over four years. On a previous occasion, Tamburella had asked his employer to “check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza”. Beyond the dispute over pizza toppings, management raised concerns about his use of foul language, communication style and what it described as an “escalation of frustration in the workplace”. The ruling also detailed an incident in April when Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand after striking a metal handrail at work. The chef had reportedly hoped to secure employer sponsorship for a visa that would allow him to remain in Australia as a permanent resident. However, following his dismissal, the restaurant discontinued the sponsorship process. Tamburella subsequently approached the Fair Work Commission, challenging his dismissal. However, the commission rejected his unfair dismissal claim because it was lodged outside the permitted timeframe. The restaurant’s managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was “more to this story than a pizza topping”. The BBC said it had contacted Tamburella for comment. On his LinkedIn profile, the chef describes himself as someone whose career has focused on “delivering exceptional food” and “improving business performance”. He also shared a post titled “letter for chefs” three months ago, centred on the theme of “respecting the ingredients”. His LinkedIn profile indicates that he now works at another restaurant in Brisbane. A BBC check found that pineapple is not included on its menu. Meanwhile, Queensland, where the restaurant was located, is regarded as Australia’s pineapple heartland and produces the country’s commercially grown pineapples. The state is also home to the Big Pineapple, a 16-metre fibreglass structure on the Sunshine Coast that has become a popular local landmark. nigeria.title: Ogun ready for State Police – Abiodun
nigeria.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun has declared his administration’s readiness to establish a state police force, describing it as a critical step towards strengthening security, protecting investments and sustaining the state’s growing economic activities. The governor also announced the immediate commencement of a social investment cash transfer programme for vulnerable residents to cushion the effects of rising food and transportation costs. Abiodun made the announcements at a town hall meeting on the 2027 budget and the 2027–2029 Medium Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) for Remo Division, held at the Akarigbo Palace, Sagamu. Speaking on the proposed establishment of state police, the governor, who chairs the Nigeria Governors’ Forum Committee on State Police, said Ogun was prepared to embrace the initiative, noting that the state’s expanding industrial and commercial activities required a more robust security framework. He declared: “I am the Chairman of the Governors’ Forum on State Police creation. Ogun State is ready for state police.” Abiodun said his administration had consistently strengthened the state’s security architecture through the provision of operational vehicles, allowances and equipment, as well as increased recruitment into the Ogun State Security Network, popularly known as Amotekun. He disclosed that Amotekun and the So-Safe Corps currently had a combined strength of about 6,000 personnel. “To protect the gains we have made, we have continued to strengthen our security architecture by providing them with vehicles, allowances and equipment. We have empowered our Amotekun and increased their recruitment,” he said. On the cash transfer initiative, the governor said the programme was designed to provide direct financial support to vulnerable households grappling with the rising cost of living, particularly food and transportation. He linked the prevailing economic pressures partly to disruptions in the global oil and gas supply chain arising from the ongoing Israel-American-Iran conflict, which he said had contributed to rising oil prices and transportation costs. “We are going to start the implementation of our social investment cash initiative. We are going to transfer cash to our people to cushion the effects of this America-Israel-Iran war,” he stated. The governor disclosed that the programme would commence immediately in Sagamu, with beneficiaries already identified and captured in the state’s database expected to receive payment alerts. He added that the initiative would subsequently be extended to other communities across Remoland and the entire state. “I am starting that today in Sagamu. I’m going into Ogijo from here. All those who have been generated to benefit will get their alerts today while I’m there. I’m going to do the same across Remoland and of course, the whole state,” he said. nigeria.title: 2027 UTME: JAMB moves to shut down substandard CBT centres
nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has moved to tighten its grip on the conduct of the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME), warning that computer-based test (CBT) centres that fail to meet its prescribed standards will be denied accreditation. The Board said only centres with adequate facilities, reliable infrastructure and the operational capacity to guarantee a credible and hitch-free examination would be approved to host candidates in the 2027 exercise. JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, gave the indication during a meeting with the leadership of the Chief External Examiners, where preparations and readiness for the accreditation exercise ahead of the 2027 UTME were reviewed. According to a post on the Board’s official X handle on Thursday, the meeting was part of efforts to strengthen examination administration and ensure strict compliance with established operational standards. The Board said the accreditation exercise would serve as a critical screening mechanism to prevent inadequately equipped centres from participating in the examination, thereby protecting candidates from avoidable disruptions and compromising examination conditions. Reiterating its position, JAMB declared that accreditation would not be automatic for CBT centres seeking to participate in the exercise. “Only centres that meet JAMB’s standards will be accredited to host the examination. For candidates, that means a fair and secure place to sit the UTME, wherever they write it,” the Board stated. The development signals JAMB’s determination to strengthen the credibility of the UTME by ensuring that candidates, irrespective of their examination locations, have access to a secure, reliable and conducive testing environment. The strict accreditation regime is also expected to address operational shortcomings that have historically threatened the smooth conduct of computer-based examinations, including inadequate facilities and poor technical readiness. With preparations for the 2027 UTME gathering momentum, the Board maintained that compliance with its accreditation requirements would remain non-negotiable for all CBT centres seeking approval to participate in the nationwide examination. nigeria.title: British woman, unborn baby die in Nigeria; family seeks help to bring bodies home
nigeria.description: A 40-year-old British woman who relocated to Nigeria to start a new life with her husband has died alongside her unborn baby after developing sepsis. Claire Chadwick, who was 37 weeks pregnant, reportedly suffered septic shock after her baby girl died in the womb. In a report by Daily Mail UK, Chadwick had moved to Nigeria to be with her husband, Ibrahim, and was expecting their first child together. She had built a social media following of thousands through videos documenting their relationship, religious beliefs and food challenges on TikTok and Instagram. Her death has left her family devastated, with her sister, Shannon, revealing that she is survived by her 19-year-old son in Wales, her husband and other relatives. Describing her late sister, Shannon said Claire was a funny and fiercely strong-minded woman who lived life on her own terms. “She was a woman who lived her life in her own way and she will leave a lasting impression on everyone who knew her,” she told WalesOnline. The family has since launched a GoFundMe campaign with a target of £10,000 to repatriate Claire and her unborn daughter to the United Kingdom for burial. Explaining the purpose of the fundraiser, Shannon said the family wanted to bring both bodies home so they could be laid to rest with dignity and surrounded by their loved ones. “More than anything, we want them both returned so they can be laid to rest with dignity, surrounded by the family who love them,” she said. The fundraiser has attracted widespread support, with Shannon describing the response as overwhelming. She also expressed gratitude to REST, a charity that supports families dealing with the sudden or tragic deaths of loved ones abroad. Tributes have also poured in from friends and well-wishers, who remembered Chadwick as a kind, caring and cheerful woman. One supporter recalled knowing her from childhood and described her as lovely, while another said she was devastated by the loss, remembering her as someone who always made people laugh. The family hopes to raise enough money to bring Claire and her unborn daughter back to the UK. Nafiu Bala Gombe, National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has declared that no political party leader is above the party’s constitution, following the Federal High Court judgment on the party’s leadership dispute. Gombe said the judgment reinforced the principle that leadership positions in political parties must emerge through lawful and constitutionally recognised procedures, not imposition or political expediency, insisting that courts must intervene when parties disregard their own rules. In a statement reacting to the judgment in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, involving him, the ADC and four others, Gombe commended the trial judge for what he described as an independent, impartial and courageous handling of the politically sensitive dispute. “With profound respect for the Bench, and with a deep sense of duty to the administration of justice in Nigeria, I most respectfully commend the Federal High Court and the trial Judge for the independent, impartial, and intellectually rigorous manner in which His Lordship handled and determined the above-referenced matter,” he said. Describing the case as a major test of judicial independence, Gombe said it raised critical questions about party autonomy, internal democracy, constitutional supremacy and the regulatory responsibilities of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). “By subjecting the question of leadership emergence to constitutional and statutory scrutiny, rather than to political expediency, His Lordship affirmed a foundational principle of Nigerian jurisprudence: political parties are not above their own constitutions, and the Electoral Act is not a mere suggestion,” he stated. On the obligation of political parties to obey their internal rules, Gombe said courts had a duty to intervene where established procedures were disregarded. “Where a party’s constitution prescribes a procedure for succession and leadership, that procedure must be obeyed. nigeria.title: Zidane’s son dropped from Algeria squad for AFCON qualifiers
nigeria.description: Algeria goalkeeper Luca Zidane was left out of the national team squad on Thursday ahead of two Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Togo, coach Brahim Hemdani said. Zidane, 28, has recently been missing from the Algerian team, owing to injury and a two-game suspension over scuffles during an AFCON game against Nigeria in January. But his exclusion was “based on sporting criteria”, Hemdani told journalists. “I need to have three goalkeepers who were getting as much playing time as possible.” Hemdani called up USM Alger goalkeeper Oussama Benbot alongside Melvin Mastil of Swiss club Lausanne-Sport and Abdelatif Ramdane of MC Alger. Zidane, a son of French football icon Zinedine Zidane, joined the Fennecs after changing his sporting nationality in September 2025 to represent Algeria, where his family has roots. The Leganes goalkeeper’s absence came as a surprise, along with that of Manchester City defender Rayan Ait-Nouri. Ait-Nouri had been sent home in September following a reported dispute with the coaching staff during a match against Zambia. But Hemdani said there had been “no problem” after his choice not to include the left-back in his next 26-man squad, adding that there were “criteria for inclusion”. “However, anything is possible in the future, and no one has been permanently excluded,” the coach said. Algeria are set to face Togo on November 14 and 17. They have four points from two games and are currently top of AFCON qualification Group I, which includes Zambia and Burundi. nigeria.title: Nigerian teenager, Fawaz jailed four years for attempting to steal Porsche in London
nigeria.description: A 19-year-old Nigerian teenager, Fawaz Oyedeji, has been sentenced to four years in prison in the United Kingdom for attempting to steal a £72,500 Porsche Cayenne using an imitation firearm. Oyedeji, who is from Greenwich, London, posed as a prospective buyer after responding to an online advertisement for the luxury sports utility vehicle. He arranged to meet the seller at the victim’s home in Southwark on Tuesday, March 18, to inspect the vehicle. After the victim showed him around the Porsche, the pair entered the front seats to discuss the sale. Oyedeji then produced what appeared to be a firearm, pointed it at the seller and demanded the car keys. However, the victim resisted and fought back, forcing Oyedeji to abandon the attempt and flee from the scene. The police were subsequently alerted and launched an investigation into the incident. Detectives traced the phone used to arrange the vehicle inspection to Oyedeji, establishing that it had been in the vicinity of both his home address and the scene of the attempted robbery. Investigators also obtained CCTV footage showing his movements shortly before and after the incident. Clothing matching what the suspect wore during the attempted robbery was also recovered by officers. Oyedeji was arrested at his home on Leonard Robbins Path within 38 hours of the offence. A jury at the Inner London Crown Court found him guilty after just 26 minutes of deliberation on Wednesday, November 4. He was subsequently sentenced to four years’ imprisonment. Detective Constable Alex Long, who led the investigation, praised the victim for resisting the armed robbery and cooperating with investigators. “The victim showed immense courage by refusing to hand over his keys despite being threatened with what appeared to be a genuine firearm,” Long said. He added that CCTV footage, digital records and forensic evidence helped detectives build a strong case that secured Oyedeji’s conviction. The detective also urged people buying or selling vehicles privately to take necessary precautions, advising them to leave if a transaction appeared suspicious and call emergency services when necessary. nigeria.title: 2027: Obi’s wave doesn’t exist again, he has nothing to offer — Wike
nigeria.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has dismissed the political support behind Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying the wave that propelled him in the 2023 election no longer exists. Wike also described Obi as a dramatist, insisting that the former Anambra State governor had nothing to offer Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. The minister spoke on Thursday during his monthly media chat in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, where he questioned the prospects of the NDC presidential ticket featuring Obi and former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso. “All this so-called Obi kererenke doesn’t exist again. I have killed it,” Wike said. He argued that the political circumstances that helped Obi secure significant support in the 2023 presidential election had changed. “Nigerians know that Obi has nothing to offer, he is a dramatist. You were there when Soludo exposed him,” the minister said. In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday through its Office of the Spokesperson, the coalition accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of benefiting from what it described as a systematic effort to weaken opposition parties. CUPP alleged that the judgment was part of a broader attempt to undermine opposition political structures and create conditions for a one-party state. The coalition also expressed concern over the role of the judiciary, arguing that the ruling raised questions about the courts’ responsibility to protect democratic rights and political participation. The statement read in part: “CUPP views this controversial judgment not as an isolated legal dispute, but as part of a well-choreographed, state-sponsored onslaught aimed at wiping out viable opposition parties and turning Nigeria into a one-party state.” It further alleged that sections of the judiciary had failed to adequately protect the interests of citizens and the electoral process. CUPP also accused the APC-led government of relying on legal technicalities to challenge opposition candidates and party leadership structures, saying such developments could restrict political competition and undermine public confidence in the electoral system. The coalition warned that the judiciary must remain guided by the Constitution and the interests of Nigerians rather than political considerations. “The judiciary must remember that its allegiance belongs to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, not to the political actors of the day. CUPP declared solidarity with the ADC and other opposition groups, saying it would continue to defend democratic participation and political pluralism. nigeria.title: Tinubu Congratulates Flamingos, Backs Team To Win U-17 World Cup

Go for the trophy, Flamingos!” he added. business.title: Core Scientific (CORZ) to Exit Bitcoin Mining by Year-End as Colocation Hits $215 Million
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Core Scientific (CORZ) to Exit Bitcoin Mining by Year-End as Colocation Hits $215 Million Core Scientific will complete its exit from bitcoin mining by year-end and enter 2027 as a pure-play high-density colocation provider, management said on Thursday’s third-quarter earnings call, capping a pivot that has already cut the company’s mining fleet nearly in half. Chief Financial Officer Jim Nygaard told investors the company expects to “complete the wind-down during the fourth quarter.” Chief Executive Officer Adam Sullivan put the same end date more bluntly: “We expect to complete our exit from Bitcoin mining by year end.” The comments landed alongside a results release filed with the SEC that shows how far the shift has already gone. Colocation revenue climbed nearly 60% sequentially to $215.4 million in the quarter ended Sept. 30, the earnings exhibit shows. Digital asset self-mining revenue fell to $12.3 million, down about 79% from $57.4 million a year earlier. Hosted mining for third parties added just $5.2 million. Of $232.9 million in total revenue, colocation now accounts for roughly 92%. Self-mining posted a $7.5 million gross loss in the quarter. Colocation gross profit was $128.4 million, a 60% margin. Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled sequentially to $133.6 million, with the margin expanding to 57% from 25%. Mining shrinks as AI leases fill the floor Nygaard said Core Scientific had nearly 50% fewer miners online at the end of September than at year-end 2025. The company has been repurposing power and floor space under long-term customer agreements for AI and high-performance computing workloads, a process its investor materials describe as continuing “as circumstances allow.” That path is not unique among public miners. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate Greece’s parliament approved on Thursday a bill that imposes a 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies, the first comprehensive legal framework for taxing crypto assets in the country. Cryptocurrency capital gains of up to €500 ($563) a year will be exempt from the new tax, the bill says. For bitcoin holders in Greece, that threshold is a small buffer, not a carve-out for larger positions. “Further implementation directives will be published in the coming weeks, which will also define transparency and audit rules,” a senior finance ministry official told Reuters . An earlier draft circulated in October had floated a 15% rate. The version lawmakers passed lands five points lower, while keeping the €500 annual exemption that was already in that proposal. What the levy covers for bitcoin holders The tax is set to apply from Jan. 1, 2027, Greek coverage of the finance ministry bill says. It is levied on the net gain — the difference between the acquisition price and the transfer price — not on the full sale proceeds. Trading fees and other costs tied to the deal can factor into that calculation. A taxable transfer is not limited to selling for euros. Using cryptocurrency to buy goods or services, or contributing it to cover or increase company capital, can also crystallize a gain under the new rules. That matters for anyone in Greece who pays a merchant in bitcoin rather than converting first. Simply holding bitcoin while its euro value rises does not, by itself, create a tax bill. Crypto-to-crypto swaps, such as bitcoin for another token, are treated as non-taxable events in the explanatory material that accompanied the bill, matching the approach France has used to avoid taxing every hop between coins. Net annual gains at or below €500 are exempt. Greek analyses of the text say that once net gains clear that ceiling, the 10% rate applies to the full net gain for the year, not only the slice above €500. Losses above €500 in a tax year may be carried forward for up to five years and offset only against future crypto capital gains. Purchases of crypto assets are also being pulled into Greece’s existing “source of funds” checks from 2027, so buyers may need to show that the euros used to acquire bitcoin or other tokens came from declared income or other lawful capital. The rule does not add a separate purchase tax; it widens the audit trail around how coins were funded. Rates on cryptocurrency gains typically run from about 8% to 30% across member states and are usually levied on capital gains, the finance ministry official said. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Pushes 22% Crypto Tax to 2029 in Fourth Delay, Offers Three-Year Loss Carryforward South Korea’s government plans to push back its tax on cryptocurrency gains by another two years to 2029, Finance and Economy Minister Lee Hyeong-il said Thursday, in what would be the fourth delay since the levy was written into law. The tax is scheduled to take effect in January. To postpone it, the National Assembly must amend the Income Tax Act before then, and Lee said the government would seek lawmakers’ approval during this year’s regular session. “It weighs heavily on me to propose another delay after the tax has already been postponed three times,” Lee said at a press briefing in Seoul. Korea legislated the tax in 2020 for a 2022 start. It was then pushed to 2023, 2025 and 2027 as officials conceded that tax systems and investor protections were not ready. Waiting on U.S. data The main reason for the new delay is data on overseas trading. When investors move tokens bought abroad onto a Korean exchange, the exchange may have no record of the purchase price needed to calculate a taxable gain. That gap closes in 2029, when Korea and the United States begin exchanging information under the OECD-backed Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, or CARF. Introducing the tax before then could put Korea’s domestic crypto market at a disadvantage, the government said . “Once we begin receiving cryptocurrency transaction data from the United States in 2029, we will have enough information to tax investors who use US exchanges on the same basis as those who trade in the domestic market,” Lee said. The government also cited the need to align the tax with the proposed Digital Asset Act, which would set rules for digital asset businesses and strengthen investor protection. Korea’s broader crypto rulebook has been moving on several fronts , including a Bank of Korea push to write stablecoins into foreign exchange law. Exchanges, investors and lawmakers had pressed for more time, with exchanges saying unclear reporting requirements held up system development and testing. Individuals would pay 22%, including local income tax, on annual net income above 2.5 million won, or about $1,869, from selling or lending virtual assets such as bitcoin. What is new is a proposed three-year loss carryforward. Under current law, only losses from the same year can offset gains, so an investor could owe tax in a profitable year even after losing more the year before. Under the proposal, losses realized in 2029 could offset gains through 2032. Losses realized before the tax takes effect would not be eligible, the government said , citing the volatility of crypto prices as the reason for the change. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. entertainment.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. Former Board Member Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa urged guests to look past the continent’s challenges and toward its potential and to use the days ahead to turn conversations into partnerships. The task is to use that small pool to unlock far larger sources, such as pension funds and fixed-income assets, so money reaches businesses that create jobs. sports.description: Tottenham chief executive Vinai Venkatesham believes the club is heading in the right direction again and has outlined an ultimate objective of winning the Premier League . Spurs narrowly avoided a disastrous drop to the Championship during a tumultuous 2025-26 campaign that saw long-standing chairman Daniel Levy leave, while Thomas Frank and Igor Tudor were both sacked before Roberto De Zerbi secured survival on the final day. A summer of heavy spending followed, bringing 10 new signings and several high-profile departures. After a sluggish opening to the campaign, Tottenham travel to Leeds on Saturday on the back of three straight victories. Speaking on The Sports Agents Podcast, Venkatesham said: "We’ve had three better results in a row, but there is nothing here where we think, ‘oh we’ve cracked it’ and we’re right at the start of this journey of where we are going to. Roberto De Zerbi's side have won three games in a row (PA) "There will be good moments this season and bad moments this season, but I firmly believe we’re on the right track to where we want to get to. "Ultimately, I guess the best way to answer your question (about targets) is what are we here for? We’re here to win, right? The people that we’ve attracted to the football club, the long list of people, everyone is here to win. "If you work for Tottenham, when we talk about being here to win, that means we’re here to win the Premier League. That’s what this football club wants to do. It wants to win the Premier League and it wants to be consistent in the Champions League and ultimately win the Champions League. "Can I tell you what year that’s going to happen in? Obviously I can’t but that’s what we’re aiming for and that’s what I want every single person that works for this club to think about every single day." sports.description: Motorsport photo 2026 Formula 1 champion Kimi Antonelli has opened up about his recent visit to Ayrton Senna's family home ahead of this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix. The Mercedes driver went to Fazenda Dois Lagos, the Senna family estate, on Tuesday, two days after clinching the F1 title in Mexico. He shared a photo of himself sitting in the Lotus 98T that Senna raced in 1986 and thanked the family for an "unforgettable day". Speaking to the media at Interlagos, Antonelli said the experience had been even more emotional than he expected it to be. "I was truly emotional," the Italian said. "A very, very special day, a day that I will remember forever. That's why I will always be thankful and grateful towards the Senna family for allowing me to see that, and to even sit in the car, which was very special. "It was an amazing day. I actually didn't want to leave. I tried to stay as long as I could there, because it was such a nice experience. The Senna family was very open about showing places where Ayrton used to spend most of his time. It was crazy to think. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes "When I was there, I was like, 'Wow, Ayrton was actually here. He was spending time in his room.' It was very emotional and a very, very special day." Antonelli was joined for the visit by his father, Marco, as well as Senna's nephew Bruno and nieces Bianca and Lalalli. Bruno later thanked the 20-year-old on Instagram for "the karting lesson", with the estate having its own kart track. He will also race this weekend with a special tribute helmet to Senna, 35 years since the Brazilian's first home win at Interlagos in 1991. "This one means a lot to me," Antonelli posted on social media alongside the special helmet design. "My special helmet for the weekend! A tribute to my idol and Brazil. sports.title: A.J. Brown knee injury ‘raises some concerns’ about Patriots future
sports.description: The New England Patriots trading first- and fourth-round draft picks to the Philadelphia Eagles for wide receiver A.J. Brown was a gamble. On the one hand, he was a proven No. 1 wide receiver capable of adding a new level of playmaking ability to what was one of the best offenses in football in 2025. On the other hand, he was heading into his age-29 season off of his least productive season in four years. Eight weeks into the season, the gamble has not paid off. Brown has appeared in just three games so far, catching nine passes for 101 yards. A bigger concern than his output, however, is his injury situation. Not only did he spend four games on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain, he also is currently dealing with a knee injury that has forced him to miss four straight practices and last Sunday’s win in Miami. While that knee injury has not prompted another move to IR, Brown’s short-term availability has been impacted. And beyond that, there are questions about his long-term outlook as well as addressed by ESPN’s Adam Schefter on Thursday morning. “Let’s go back to the offseason, when Philadelphia was shopping A.J. Brown and they were talking to teams,” Schefter said. “One of the reasons that I believe there wasn’t more interest was there were some teams that had some questions about his knee. In fact, when they were advanced discussions for a trade with the Los Angeles Rams that was at one point close to being completed … I think the Rams had some concerns about his knee. The concerns that other teams have had have now manifested themselves in New England this season. “It flared up. … The knee held him out last week, and the knee is threatening to hold him out this week. It’s a knee that I think raises some concerns as to how long he’s going to keep playing here in New England, and producing at a high level.” More Here: pic.twitter.com/qJbKrjlrr4 — Carlos A. Lopez (@LosTalksPats) November 5, 2026 Worries about Brown’s knee are nothing new. Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf himself spoke about them earlier this year. “It’s a factor, but we examined him,” Wolf said back in June. “He’s got a knee that has some wear and tear that we were aware of. Our training staff and medical staff signed off on it.” Regardless of his current availability issues, the Patriots moving on from Brown in the near future is not expected. His contract structure alone would likely prevent such a move from happening: if released next offseason, for example, New England would take on a dead cap charge of almost $26 million. For the time being, though, Brown remains with the Patriots and part of their 53-man roster. How quickly he can return to the field will be seen, though; one line of thinking is that he might be kept out through the team’s trip to Germany next week and into the Week 11 bye to get fully ready for the stretch run. Whether he will be, only time will tell.

technology.title: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets
technology.description: With a huge and still-growing catalog of exoplanets, researchers are anxious to take the next steps: trying to infer what conditions are like on them, either by imaging them directly or by capturing the light that has passed through their atmosphere. Both are substantial challenges, given the presence of stars that are far, far brighter than light that has come to us via the planet. While telescopes can be fitted with devices called coronagraphs that block out much of a star's light, there are limits to their effectiveness, caused by noise from subtle variations in the telescope's configuration and pointing between observations. Now, researchers have developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the telescope in a way that allows us to better model these differences, producing low-noise imaging of exoplanets. Point spreads Central to this work is the concept of a point spread function. If you use a telescope to image a single point of light, it will not appear that way in the actual image. Instead, it will be slightly blurry and spread out, due to imperfections in the telescope hardware and the limits of our ability to keep it pointed accurately through the time it takes to image something. The mathematical description of how a telescope distorts a point of light is called its point spread function. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Get root on a musl Linux system by slamming it with an overly long password
technology.description: On certain Linux systems, an attacker could gain root access by entering a password longer than 256 bytes. The vulnerability, dubbed *sshole by Wakefield researcher Özgün Kültekin, who discovered it, can only be exploited in very specific conditions. The flaw affects certain Linux systems using musl libc instead of the traditional GNU C library, and even then only those running OpenSSH's secure shell daemon without Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) and with password authentication enabled. If those conditions are met, and at least one other account has a valid password hash, accounts that shouldn't accept passwords, such as root, key-only deployment users, and LDAP users, may be accessed by supplying a password between 257 and 1,024 characters. The targeted accounts must have an asterisk (*) in their password field, and direct root login remains subject to OpenSSH's configuration. That might seem niche, but sorry: It’s not. Musl libc is common in embedded Linux systems due to its low footprint. More critically than that, it's also the standard C library for Alpine Linux, which provides official cloud images for both AWS and Azure. Some Alpine systems running in those environments may therefore be vulnerable, depending on their configuration. Dawn of the *sshole The vulnerability in OpenSSH on musl-based Linux systems dates back to 2016, but Kültekin explains that its roots go back much further – to the BSD Unix era, actually. In 1980, Sun Microsystems cofounder and BSD Unix heavyweight Bill Joy was involved in the development of BSD Unix, whose password file contained a single asterisk in the /etc/passwd entry for the daemon user. The asterisk wasn't a password hash and effectively disabled password authentication for that account. Nowadays, password hashes typically live in /etc/shadow and contain hashed information that the system uses to verify a plaintext password entered by a user. Asterisks are still present for accounts that aren't supposed to accept password logins, but as Kültekin explains in his writeup, that isn't exactly a foolproof way to keep people out. The crypt() function, which generates password hashes for comparison with stored values, can return NULL if it can't compute a hash. Applications that fail to check that result may crash. Musl libc's developers instead chose to return a single character for certain failures, and they picked the asterisk. Musl also added SHA-512-based password hashing around the same time, which Kültekin notes gets slower the longer a password is, potentially leading to denial of service if someone floods a server with a super-long password. Musl capped passwords at 256 bytes, and you can likely see where this is going. In 2016, OpenSSH introduced a workaround to prevent attackers from enumerating valid account names through SSH. science.title: Blue Origin announces 3rd stage for its powerful New Glenn rocket —and a new engine
science.description: null Blue Origin's big rocket is getting a little bigger. Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible. The stage, called the GS3, "enhances New Glenn's capabilities," Blue Origin said in a blog post today . "The third stage enables direct deployment of satellite constellations to GEO [ geostationary orbit ] and supports heavy-lift science and exploration missions to the moon and deep space." Illustration of the variants of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, with the new GS3 third stage now in the mix. (Image credit: Blue Origin) New Glenn is a two-stage vehicle at the moment. Its reusable first stage is powered by seven of Blue Origin's BE-4 engines, and its second stage features two of the company's BE-3Us. The rocket stands 322 feet (98 meters) tall and can haul 14.3 tons (13 metric tons) to geostationary transfer orbit (GTO) and 50 tons (45 metric tons) to low Earth orbit (LEO). These are the specs for the standard, or "7x2," version of New Glenn. Last year, Blue Origin announced that it's developing a super-heavy variant known as the 9x4, because it will feature nine first-stage BE-4s and four upper-stage BE-3Us. The 9x4 will be nearly 400 feet (122 m) tall, and it will be able to loft 15.4 tons (14 metric tons) to GTO and 77 tons (70 metric tons) to LEO, according to Blue Origin . Another setback came just a month later: On May 28, New Glenn exploded on the pad during a routine engine test at Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station . Blue Origin has been working ever since to rebuild the pad and get New Glenn ready for its fourth flight, which is expected to occur late this year. Blue Origin tests a tank for the GS3 third stage of its New Glenn rocket at its Launch Site One in Texas. (Image credit: Blue Origin) We now know that Blue Origin has also been working on the GS3 while those repairs were underway. science.title: The economic benefits of the covid vaccines may be double what we thought
science.description: The covid-19 vaccines were costly to produce, but paid for themselves many times over Paul Christian Gordon / Alamy The covid-19 vaccines may have provided health and economic benefits worth up to $64.3 trillion in the first year alone – almost double an earlier estimate. Previously, researchers calculated that the $79.4 billion invested in developing covid-19 vaccines saw a return of between $4.8 trillion and $37.9 trillion globally in the first 12 months after their rollout. But now, a reanalysis of the data suggests it is actually between $6.43 trillion and $64.3 trillion. This means that for every $1 spent on the vaccines’ development, between $59.70 and $809 was gained in that year. “It is great to finally see this research published to demonstrate the enormous health and financial benefits gained from covid-19 vaccines, in comparison to the costs that went into their development and delivery,” says Hallie Benjamin at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. Read more Does each new covid-19 variant pose a significant threat? The $6.43 trillion figure is based on a cost-effectiveness analysis that is generally used in the health sector and factors in quality of life, while the $64.3 trillion figure is based on a cost-benefit analysis used in the public sector. Advertisement Both include data from 173 countries on averted hospitalisations, productivity losses and lives saved. For instance, one of the estimates Benjamin and her colleagues used came from modelling that suggested the vaccines prevented 14 million to 20 million deaths in their first year. The initial $4.8 trillion and $37.9 trillion figures were released when the research was in a preprint stage, before it had been peer-reviewed. “We made many changes throughout the peer-review process that strengthened the quality of our findings,” says Benjamin. The researchers originally used the Value of Statistical Life Years, which considers how many years a person would be likely to live because of the vaccine, a figure that would be lower if someone was older. As part of the peer-review process, they were advised to use the Value of Statistical Life. Team member Mark Jit at New York University says this treats life spans more equally and is aligned with recommendations for valuing mortality-risk reductions. Free newsletter Sign up to Health Check Sign up to newsletter The cost-benefit analysis figure also increased significantly due to a change from calculating the economic value of avoiding a death, says Jit. But the returns weren’t equally distributed. The researchers found that the vaccines had the highest returns in richer countries. This was probably because poorer countries accessed them later, so fewer lives were saved and fewer productivity and healthcare costs were averted, says Jit. The results are “a message about the need for being able to distribute the vaccines fairly to the people most in need around the world”, he says. Covid raises risk of heart issues in children

science.title: Tomb in Siberia reveals humans were using cannabis 2800 years ago
science.description: Researchers excavate a burial mound containing horse and human bones along with cannabis seeds Frozen Corpses Golden Treasures, T.Wallace & G. Casp A hair found in a 2800-year-old tomb in Siberia has yielded the earliest definitive evidence of cannabis being used as a psychoactive drug. But the history of such use is likely to go back much further. Genomic studies suggest that the domestication of cannabis plants ( Cannabis sativa ) was happening in China about 12,000 years ago , with people potentially exploiting it for oil and hemp fibre. Archaeological sites with artefacts made from hemp dating to 7500 years ago have been found in China and Japan . The earliest firm evidence of the plant’s use as a drug had been chemical traces on wooden braziers in China that implied humans were “smoking” cannabis 2500 years ago as part of funeral rites. Read more How a surge in ancient plagues 5000 years ago shaped humanity Now, Gino Caspari at the University of Bern in Switzerland and his colleagues have pushed the date back another 300 years with a find at the Tunnug 1 burial mound in the Uyuk Valley of southern Siberia. Advertisement The royal burial mound dates to the time of the Scythians, nomads renowned for their military skills and horseback archery who spread across a huge swathe of Eurasia. In an excavation trench at the centre of the mound, Caspari and his colleagues recovered almost 1000 whole cannabis seeds. Radiocarbon dating indicated that they were deposited around the start of the 8th century BC, some 2800 years ago. He says we can’t say how the person consumed the drug – it might have been smoked or the seeds could have just been ingested.
